subject: Urgent: Quantisys production latency surge — exec sync & mitigation plan
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia@quantisys.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Quantisys SRE <sre@quantisys.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: High tail latency observed on production calls (Quantisys)

Hannah —

We started seeing sharp p95/p99 spikes for our checkout API around 14:30 PDT. Error rates briefly climbed to ~7% and several checkout sessions timed out. This is affecting roughly 3% of production traffic but disproportionately impacts large batched requests.

Relevant notes:
- SRE traces show occasional 503s from the Redwood hosted endpoint and long stalls at the token-generation stage.
- Our dashboard (attached) shows tail latency drifting from ~180ms to ~2.2s for long sequences.
- We captured request IDs: qnt-req-8a3f, qnt-req-8a46 — samples attached.

Can you confirm if anything changed on your side? We have a hard SLA window and this is customer-visible. If this requires exec attention, please escalate.

Thanks,
Olivia Park
Head of Platform — Quantisys
[Attachment: quantisys_slo_dashboard.png (image/png)]
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@quantisys.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency observed on production calls (Quantisys)

Olivia —

Thanks for the quick heads-up and the dashboard. I'm escalating this to infra and our incident leads. We're treating this as high priority. Immediate plan:

1) Aditya/infra to look for runtime OOMs / GPU memory churn and check for recent kernel or rollout changes.
2) Monica/CS will keep Quantisys updated and capture impact for SRE request.
3) If we confirm p99 regressions tied to runtime, we'll schedule an exec bridge at next availability (within 2 hours).

Olivia, can you share a couple of example request payloads and the exact request IDs for the slow traces?

Hannah
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Initial triage: signs point to GPU memory fragmentation / OOM cascade

Team —

Quick summary of what I'm seeing from the runtime for the Quantisys tenant (logs attached):
- Immediately prior to the spike there are a series of KV cache misses and repeated small OOM retries on a subset of worker pods.
- Kernel traces show repeated allocation failures and subsequent fallback to slower host-side memcpy paths which explains the 2s stalls.
- There's evidence of slab fragmentation on the accelerator; GC isn't reclaiming fast enough and we're seeing short-lived process restarts.

Evidence: redwood_runtime_logs_qnt-4392.txt (attached) contains repeated patterns: "alloc failed" -> "retrying" -> "fallback memcpy" -> "response delayed". Also attaching a heap snapshot from one affected worker: heap-dump-20270418.tar.gz (small)

Immediate mitigations I can try now (low-risk):
- Reduce default sequence length cap for Quantisys to 512 for affected routes (will lower QoS for very long prompts but should cut p99).
- Temporarily route a small percentage of traffic to a different model variant (quant-v1-small) that uses less GPU memory.
- Increase aggressive KV-caching TTL for repeated prefixes.

If those don't help within 30–45 mins we should convene an exec bridge and consider rolling back recent runtime kernel changes from this morning (if any).

Aditya
Sr. SRE, Runtime — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_runtime_logs_qnt-4392.txt]
[Attachment: heap-dump-20270418.tar.gz]
From: Paul Chen <paul.chen@quantisys.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Park <olivia@quantisys.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency observed on production calls (Quantisys)

Hannah / Aditya —

Thanks for the fast follow. Our checkout pipeline is time-sensitive; even a 1.5s tail causes checkout abandonment. We do have a few high-token batched requests (some automated invoice-generation jobs) — I can add routing on our side to avoid them but would prefer Redwood to keep production stable.

We also need a very rough ETA on mitigation. If you land on a mitigation that requires a route change, please include steps we should expect (any SDK changes, config toggles).

Paul Chen
SRE Manager — Quantisys
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency observed on production calls (Quantisys)

Folks —

I support Aditya's mitigations. My recommended immediate actions we can execute in the next 20–30 minutes:

1) Canary route 10% of Quantisys production traffic to quant-v1-small in the same region (no SDK change required; transparent routing).
2) Enforce a soft request-level sequence cap of 512 tokens on the hosted route for Quantisys with a 503-to-fallback policy for >512.
3) Enable aggressive KV cache for top 20 prefixes observed in their traffic for 6 hours.
4) Start a controlled pod drain/restart sequence to defragment memory on the affected pool; do 1 node at a time.

I'll standby to own the rollback plan if the kernel patch from 08:40 this morning is implicated. If mitigations reduce p99 within 45m, no exec bridge needed. Otherwise, schedule an exec bridge at 17:15 PDT.

Rishi
VP, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@quantisys.ai>, Paul Chen <paul.chen@quantisys.ai>, Quantisys SRE <sre@quantisys.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Executive summary: Quantisys latency surge & next steps

Olivia / Paul —

This morning's incident (April 18, 14:30 PDT) produced a transient but customer-visible increase in p95/p99 for Quantisys. Quick executive summary and actions taken:

- Root cause (initial): GPU memory fragmentation leading to intermittent allocation failures and fallback memcpy paths in the inference runtime. Evidence: repeated allocation failure logs and heap snapshots from affected workers.
- Customer impact: ~3% of sessions saw >1.5s latency; error rate spiked to ~7% for ~25 minutes. The worst impact was on large batched jobs.
- Immediate mitigations applied by Redwood: canary 10% of traffic to quant-v1-small; sequence cap to 512 for affected routes; aggressive KV cache for top prefixes; controlled node drain to defragment pool. These reduced p99 within 35 minutes.
- Longer-term remediation: engineering will run a focused patch for slab allocator tuning and schedule a controlled trial of a new kernel build in our staging fleet. We'll also propose an autoscaling/eviction policy change to avoid cascading restarts under similar patterns.
- Customer ask: Quantisys requested an ETA and asked about potential credits. Monica will follow up on the credits/contractual impact.

Next steps / owners:
- Engineering (Aditya/Rishi): perform root-cause RCA and draft a patch plan (ETA 72 hours).
- CS (Monica): quantify business impact and own the credit conversation with Quantisys (ETA 24 hours).
- Execs (Lauren/Hannah): monitor for regressions and approve any cross-tenant kernel rollbacks.

Olivia / Paul, we appreciate the escalation and your artifacts — this helped us converge quickly. Monica will reach out within 24 hours with a compensation recommendation.

Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

[This message was sent as an executive summary to Quantisys and internal leadership.]
